thread.title: Are Dividend Stocks Helping In Stock Market Correction?

author: DOUG ROGERS
title: Are Dividend Stocks Helping In Stock Market Correction?
text:
The top-performing ETFs that invest in dividend stocks this year have had a rough month amid the stock market correction, with several of them falling as much or more than the S&P 500.
X High-quality dividend stocks, those with strong earnings and solid balance sheets, often fall less than highflying growth stocks in stock market corrections.
The top-performing dividend ETF this year, WisdomTree Middle East Dividend ( GULF ), fell a relatively modest 0.45% in the one-month period ended Oct. 17. That compares with a 4.97% drop by Victory Shares Dividend Accelerator ( VSDA ) and a 2.64% decline by the S&P 500, according to Morningstar Direct.
Dividend Stocks In Correction GULF has a year-to-date return of 9.41%, leading all other ETFs with dividend in their name. Top holdings include Saudi Basic Industries, up about 27% this year, Al Rajhi Bank up 40% and Qatar National Bank SAQ up 50%. But the fund, which has slipped from its Aug. 13 52-week high, has fallen further in recent days amid reports that U.S.-based Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi went missing and might have been murdered in the Saudi Consulate in Turkey.
GULF, with $17 million in assets, has a tepid three-year average annual return of 4.01%. It yields 3.97% and carries an expense ratio of 0.88%.
Fidelity High Dividend ( FDVV ) is up 7.64% YTD and has managed to limit its one-month drawdown to 2%. Top holdings include Apple ( AAPL ), yielding 1.4%, Verizon Communications ( VZ ) 4.4%, Microsoft ( MSFT ) 1.7% and Century Link ( CTL ) 10.3%. Those stocks' YTD gains range from 4% for Verizon to 32% for CenturyLink.
Verizon is a member of IBD's Dividend Leaders list , which contains stock ideas for income investors . The telecom services giant has an Earnings Per Share Rating of 66 and a Relative Price Strength Rating of 85. Verizon raised its quarterly dividend to 60.25 cents a share for shareholders of record as of Oct. 10, increasing to an annual rate of $2.41 a share. The company has a dividend growth rate of 3%.
FDVV, with $220 million in assets, has been around less than three years. It yields 3.75% and has an expense ratio of 0.29%.
Of the top-performing ETFs in the accompanying table, WisdomTree U.S. Quality Dividend Growth ( DGRW ) has the best three-year average annual return: 14.53%. Top holdings of the $2.35 billion ETF include Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), which yields 4%, Microsoft, Apple and Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ), which yields 2.6%.
Exxon is down slightly this year, while Johnson & Johnson is flat.
